MRI RIGHT KNEE

Clinical information: [Age]. Ongoing medial meniscus pain with mechanical symptoms and swelling.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the right knee performed at 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Comparison examination: Previous radiographs of bilateral knees from [Date].

FINDINGS:
There is a radial tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus measuring 0.8 cm. There are extensive degenerative changes of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus with extensive apical fraying. There is a focal oblique tear involving the posterior horn and posterior aspect of the body of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface.

There is a chronic tearing of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is a T2 hyperintensity within the midportion of the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 0.4 x 0.3 cm representing a small intraligamentous ganglion.

There is mild thickening of the proximal medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament. Otherwise the collateral ligaments are intact. The extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There is a focal severe chondrosis involving the weightbearing zone and posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle with focal deep cartilage defect and small adjacent cystic changes. There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial femorotibial joint compartment. There is a mild superficial chondral disease involving the patellofemoral joint. There are focal small osteophytes at the inner aspect of the intercondylar notch

There is a mild anterior tibial translation [9 mm]. The no acute bony contusions. There is a mild joint effusion with reactive synovial thickening. There are multiple intra-articular bodies, for example posterior to the distal attachment of the posterior cruciate ligament measuring 0.6 x 0.4 cm. There is a large (2.0 x 0.8 cm), well-corticated bone fragment adjacent to the posterolateral aspect of the tibial plateau, representing another intra-articular body.

There is a low volume Baker's cyst. Small cluster of cysts in the popliteal fossa measuring a maximum of 10 mm AP by 20 mm transverse radiology a of a of alcohol

The visualized muscle bulk is unremarkable.

Conclusion:
1. Degenerative radial tear of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Underlying severe degenerative changes of the lateral meniscus with apical fraying.
2. Oblique tear at the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface.
3. Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. No acute bony contusions.
4. Moderate femorotibial osteoarthritis with severe chondrosis in the lateral femorotibial joint compartment as described in detail above.
5. Mild joint effusion with intra-articular bodies.
